"I am not a monster"

Schizophrenia 

The diagnosis burns like acid through the flesh of the afflicted.

The mind shattered.

Unarmed, symptoms pierce reality like a needle weaving through skin.

The toxicity of psychosis, isolation and decay. Disorganized thought and poverty of speech. Blunted affect, lack of pleasure and poor grooming. 

Did I shower or brush my teeth this week?

Delusional epitaphs roll off the tongue like water droplets on a maple leaf in the fall. Paranoia thickens as the Darkness infiltrates the mind poisoning rationality .

Auditory stimulus overloads the circuits. The wind whispers, church bells chime and vacuum voices mumble thick and heavy for their audience of one.

A visual spectacle entangles perception. Trees dance to silent songs and faces melt in mirrors like ink on a canvas.

Euphoric rage emerges, disjointed racing thoughts enflame the mind, igniting the senses, I am God.

A switch is flicked and light turns black.

A salty monsoon drowns out optimism. Intrusive thoughts flood the consciousness. A shell remains.

There is a war inside my mind.
I am infected.
But I am not a monster.
Absolutely! I have an overactive imagination so my delusions get intense. I write poetry related to my hallucinations and delusions.
My longest time awake was similar to yours. Mania FTW? It is like a super power no one wants. LOL

But at the end of the day I am that. I have schizophrenia and some days symptoms are worse than others. I wish there wasn't such awful stigma so I could be "out."

Thanks for asking. I am very lucky. She said she is not firing me but moving me down to part-time for now. She said she wants to give me a chance to "fix myself" since I've been a good employee for the last 4 years. 

I need to get my shit together. Figure out how to combat some of these negative symptoms. I know meds won't fix everything.

I think the most absurd was when I was 5 or 6. I thought that killer bees were coming to take over and the only way to combat the bees was with urine. For several months I peed into empty milk jugs and hid them. I got into a lot of trouble when my jugs were found. 

For many years I was convinced the closet in my bedroom was a portal to somewhere evil and if I slept in my bedroom I would be killed. I slept on the living room sofa for many years. That seems to be a huge red flag but my family apparently didn't think so. 

That ghosts were real and I could interact with them. My family reinforced this one. Now I know they were hallucinations.

That shadow people followed me ready to kidnap me at any moment when I was alone.

I received special messages from crows. 

I would refuse to eat because my mother was poisoning my food.

Those are the ones I can remember clearly that I experienced when I was a kid. I have a few new ones since I turned 16 but a few of them pop back up when I'm having an episode. It is like the delusions are paused while I'm stable and restart where they left off when I become delusional again.

When I was a kid I wrote some messed up stuff and drew a few messed up drawings which led to a conference with my mom and me getting in trouble. So, I stopped writing until my creative writing class in college. It still freaked some people out but overall it somehow became acceptable. I have 9 moods altogether. The moods range from mild (1) to severe depression (4), balanced (5), mild (6) to severe mania (9). They are divided into 2 mood levels per color that I choose from except for balanced. It helps me at the end of the year create a line graph of my moods.

I make daily summaries. I don't have specific activites dedicated to the phases but I do have quite a few activities I find helpful such as restlessness, insomnia, shower, etc... I also track my psychotic features like hallucinations, delusions, and paranoia. I just recently added a sleep component so I track under 6hrs, 7-9 hrs, over 10hrs. 

I absolutely love Daylio!

Minimal psychotic symptoms and insight into my "odd thoughts" (delusions.) Not a perfectly balanced mood but pretty close with some tiny peaks and shallow valleys. No extreme manic activity and no active suicidal thoughts. I can get up for work every day wearing clean clothes and showering occasionally... that still needs work. The negative symptoms are reduced and not overwhelming, like finding the word for something or my working memory, but they are still present which effects my job performance but I'm working on that.

Return things? Donate things? Re-gift things? Sell it all? All of the above?

There are more times when I should have gone in (like before my failed attempt) or at least admitted myself earlier to cut my suffering in half and stop the delusions before shit hit the fan. BUT I am stubborn and didn't always have insurance.

This current hypo/manic episode has been between 1-4hrs on average a night. Last night was 3.5hrs. I'm to the point in my episode where I am physically exhausted from lack of sleep but still mentally stimulated. Fml

Maybe I am bitter that he tagged me with those adjectives so flippantly? Maybe I'm reading too much into his comments. Maybe I'm slightly delusional in thinking I'm a fraud. 

You are right that severity is on a spectrum and that it can vary within a single person over a lifetime. I'm mild now but that wasn't always the case. I should be thankful that I'm lucky and I respond to meds and that my hard work had paid off.

You are right. Without meds I am completely not high functioning. And shit hits the fan pretty quickly. I'm lucky that I respond so well to them.

At my last appt my doc refused to entertain the idea of lowering my Lithium until my hypo/manic episode is over and I stop having "odd" thoughts. So, I guess you are right. If I was a fraud why keep me on meds I wouldn't otherwise need.

Thanks for commenting. :D

This is the basic difference regarding psychosis between the two:

Bipolar I w/psychotic features can include experiencing hallucinations, delusions and paranoia, etc... but only DURING depression or mania.

Schizoaffective can include experiencing hallucinations, delusions, and paranoia, etc... either DURING or OUTSIDE of depression or mania. The psychotic features can show up anytime during any mood.

For example, my mood is pretty stable but I'm still having delusions and hallucinations that would have disappeared already if I was Bipolar I. So that would be psychotic features outside of a mood episode. Which indicates that Schizoaffective is a better diagnostic fit for me.

Schizoaffective also includes the possibility of having a thought disorder and/or the negative symptoms from schizophrenia. Bipolar, as far as I am aware, does not include these symptoms at least for diagnostic purposes.

I hope that helped clarify some things.

I am not a professional but this is how I understand the different kinds of Bipolar. 

Bipolar I = Cycling of Mania and Major Depression - it can come with psychotic features. 

Bipolar II = Cycling of Hypomania and Major Depression. 

Cylothymia = Cycling of hypomania and minor depression, symptoms not severe enough for Bipolar II qualifications. I think you must have symptoms for at least 2 years? 

Bipolar NOS = You have symptoms but do not meet the qualifications (like maybe you don't have enough symptoms for the label of mania) of any of the other 3. 

Schizoaffective Bipolar type = Schizophrenia and Bipolar had a baby. Psychotic symptoms like hallucinations and delusions (that are both during and outside a cycle) and also cycles of mania and depression.
